# v3.4 — the gate lives in git

**Date:** 2026-10-30, clarified 2026-10-30, verified 2026-11-01 · **Status:** shipped (unreleased) · **Branch:** `claude/v3-6-plan-359ba7` (plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-v3-4-gate-in-git.md`)

## Goal

SSDD gets smaller and stays a framework for any harness. The review gate is
the git pre-commit, which every harness and every human already meets. The
harness hooks keep only what holds that pre-commit in the loop, what guards
an action that goes out (production, a force push), and two conveniences.
Every setting no project changed, every hook only one harness can run, and
every block on a mistake that can be undone locally either goes or becomes
a warning.

The owner's rules for this release:
- **Hard blocks only where a mistake is irreversible or outward-facing;**
  everything else warns or goes (2026-10-23).
- **Harness-neutral** (2026-10-30): "it should still be a general framework
  that fits any harness chosen", Cursor included. A harness hook may make a
  check earlier or cheaper; it never adds a rule of its own.
- **Simple and effective, not existing just to exist** (2026-10-30): a
  setting or mechanism stays only if a project used it or an incident
  needed it.

The quick fixes from the 2026-10-23 audit ship as 3.3.2, not here.

## Evidence

All checked 2026-10-30 against this branch (`7d2a6a2`), prizma and Hatedate
read-only, and the Claude Code transcripts under `~/.claude/projects` (142
project folders).

**1. Two layers run the review gate, and the harness one is most of the
code.**
- The pre-commit runs `review-gate.mjs --pre-commit`
  (`mechanisms/hooks/pre-commit:22`), which judges the index git is
  committing (`review-gate.mjs:466-469`). `install` and `update` arm it when
  they can (`armHook`, `bin/ssdd.mjs:347-354`).
- Probed in a scratch repo on git 2.54.0, with a pre-commit that prints
  `git diff --staged --name-only`: `commit -am` showed both modified files,
  `git add c.txt && git commit` showed `c.txt`, and `commit -m z b.txt`
  showed `b.txt`.
- The harness mode (`review-gate.mjs:489-750`) runs *before* the command,
  so it reads the index as it was. To make up for that, it:
  - walks `cd` / `-C` / `pushd` to find the target repo (`walk`,
    `:548-580`) and denies a call that commits to two repos (`:586`);
  - refuses staging chained before a commit unless every path is a visible,
    unrouted `git add` (`BESIDE_ADD`, `chainedAddReason`, `:620-693`);
  - refuses `commit -a/-i/-o` and `commit <pathspec>` (`:694-729`).
  It carries a 401-line test file (`review-gate.shapes.selftest.mjs`), an
  `if` filter (`docs/specs/v2.6.md` Clarify 9), and `commandStart`,
  `gitInvocation` and `isCommit` in `git-cmd.mjs` (`:35`, `:97-124`), which
  nothing else imports.
- **Its cost:** Hatedate's transcripts hold 209 calls that chain staging
  with a commit, and 78 add a routed file, so each is refused today
  (`docs/specs/v3.md:1193-1199`). Before v3 Part 3's unrouted exception, 12
  of Hatedate's 14 blocks were docs-only commits or scratch repos
  (`v3.md:1049-1051`).
- **The incident the chained-add rule answered had no pre-commit gate.**
  Hatedate's "2026-08-10 wip-commit incident" ("a chained 'git add ... &&
  git commit' with a clean index passed the empty-staged early-exit and
  committed un-reviewed", Hatedate `50207a0b`) was ported by v2.1
  (`v2.1.md:16-23`) and kept by v2.6 (Clarify 1). Hatedate's gate was
  `.claude/hooks/review-gate.mjs`, a "PreToolUse(Bash) review gate" with no
  pre-commit mode. Its `.githooks/pre-commit` (163 lines at `50207a0b`)
  checks untracked files and asset imports and has never run a review gate
  (`git log -S'review-gate' -- .githooks/pre-commit` is empty). An armed
  SSDD pre-commit closes that shape on its own.

**2. Completion stamps are Claude-only, opt-in, and unused.**
- They take SubagentStart / SubagentStop wiring
  (`adapters/claude-code/settings-hooks.json:62-81`), dispatch files under a
  lock, a transcript reader with a desktop-app special case
  (`readTranscript`, `review-gate.mjs:791-807`), a verdict parser, a model
  allow-list (`reviewerModels`, `:849`; `model-id.mjs`), and a git-guard
  rule for `stamping: "hooks"` (`git-guard.mjs:120-126`). The code is
  `review-gate.mjs:755-868`; the tests, `review-stamp.selftest.mjs` (351
  lines).
- Cursor has no subagent hooks, so Cursor repos are manual anyway
  (`docs/specs/v2.3.md`, Decision 5).
- prizma's config sets neither `stamping` nor `reviewerModels`; Hatedate has
  no `.ssdd/config.json`. v2.6 kept `reviewerModels` with "Revisit if no
  project turns it on" (Clarify 7).
- Manual stamping's misuse: 4 of 449 stamps, none since 2026-09-08
  (`docs/specs/v3.5.md`, Open 1).
- They fail silently: SubagentStart snapshots staged files only
  (`:822-826`), so a reviewer dispatched before `git add` stamps nothing,
  and the hook's stderr reaches no one (`:833-834`).

**3. A review run before `git add` counts for nothing, on any harness.**
- `--stamp` refuses a file that isn't staged (`review-gate.mjs:405-410`,
  `:417`).
- Every reviewer's default input is `git diff --staged` ("How to run" step
  1 in `reviewers/*.md`, e.g. `docs-sync-reviewer.md:34`).

**4. Any blob change voids every reviewer's stamp on the file.**
- `judge()` owes a file to each routed reviewer whose stamp key isn't the
  staged key (`review-gate.mjs:249`). The key is the blob pair
  (`stagedChanges`, `:121-129`), so a comment edit is a new key, and every
  routed reviewer re-runs on the delta (`deltaFor`, `:270`).
- prizma plan 35 task 3 was "comment/prose only" and ran five rounds
  (`prizma/.ssdd/ledgers/35-last-published-at-writer-ledger.md:16`).
- **The same ledger line cuts the other way.** Those rounds found real
  wrong claims: resilience found two more instances of the class, a round-3
  fix "carried a wrong premise" that resilience's next round caught, and
  bias-semantics and the task reviewer each found one. None came from
  docs-sync, whose contract is doc couplings, not whether a comment is true
  (`reviewers/docs-sync-reviewer.md:12-41`).
- Repeats cost in general: in Hatedate, 31% of 391 reviewer runs were
  repeats (`docs/specs/v3.md:1045-1046`), in its whole-diff-stamp era.
- The friction is comment edits in routed source. prizma's docs-sync route
  covers `^src/`, `^scripts/`, `^supabase/`, `package.json` and
  `.github/workflows/`, not `docs/`.

**5. git-guard blocks things that can be undone, and checks shapes no agent
used.**
- It blocks `git add -A` / `.` / `--all` and `git commit --amend`
  (`git-guard.mjs:129-142`). Both are local and reversible: an amend
  reaches the remote only through a force push, which the default
  `extraRules` entry blocks (`mechanisms/config.example.json`, `gitGuard`).
- A PreToolUse `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` entry
  (`settings-hooks.json:41-49`) runs git-guard on every file edit, to deny
  the file tools on `.git/ssdd-review-*` (`git-guard.mjs:58-64`). Across the
  142 transcript folders: no Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit call on a
  `review-stamp` or `review-dispatch` path (the one hit is SSDD's own
  `review-stamp.test.mjs`), and the deny message never appears. The four
  self-stamps were `--stamp` calls (`git show 68a02e9:docs/specs/v3.4.md`,
  lines 119-153).
- `core.hooksPath` detection covers the `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` /
  `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` env forms (`viaEnv`, `:112`), abbreviated write
  options such as `--unset-a` (`isWriteOption`, `:87-89`) and shell
  expansion before the key (`configWrites`, `:93-105`). The env forms
  appear in no prizma or Hatedate transcript, only in SSDD sessions
  searching for them; Hatedate's hooks never had them (`git log --all
  -G'GIT_CONFIG'` is empty there); they arrived in SSDD's v2.1 scope
  (`v2.1.md:55-56`). The abbreviation and expansion rules came "From the
  second automated review" (`35dbb04`).
- The threat-model rule they fail: "A new evasion shape is out of scope
  unless an agent was seen using it in a real project" (`docs/BACKLOG.md`;
  `v2.6.md` Clarify 3).

**6. A lint match fails the commit.** The pre-commit runs `convention-lint
--staged` under `set -e` (`pre-commit:8`), and `--staged` exits 1 on any
finding (`convention-lint.mjs:149-150`). The lint's own header calls it
"Advisory" (`:3`). A regex for a hardcoded color stops a commit.

**7. Settings no project changed.**
- prizma's config sets `routing`, `reviewGate.maxRoutedFiles` (measured on
  its history), `gitGuard` and one `lint` rule. Its `gitGuard` toggles are
  `blockBulkAdd`, `blockNoVerify` and `blockAmend`, all `true`.
- Never set by a project: `reviewGate.stamping`, `reviewerModels`,
  `reviewGate.exclude`, `preCommit.blockUntracked` (an opt-in block; the
  default is a warning), `gitGuard.blockHooksPath`, and
  `modelReview.generation`.
- `reviewGate.exclude` is a second way to say a route's own `exclude`
  (`review-gate.mjs:98-112`).
- `modelReview.generation` drives one session-view line
  (`work-state.mjs:354-359`), read from the harness payload's model, so only
  a harness that sends one sees it.
- `paths` isn't set by prizma either, but Hatedate keeps its plans in
  `.claude/plans`, so its migration may need it.

**8. New hook wiring never reaches an installed repo, and nothing says so.**
- `.claude/settings.json` is seeded: `update` "never touches them and
  prints how their templates changed instead" (`bin/ssdd.mjs:31-33`;
  `seedOne`, `:295-298`; the diff, `:569-579`).
- prizma's and Hatedate's `.claude/settings.json` wire only `PreToolUse`
  and `PostToolUse`, no `SessionStart`. Both are pre-migration.
- Cursor's `.cursor/hooks.json` is managed (`bin/ssdd.mjs:225`) and
  three-way merged by `update`, so the gap is Claude Code's seeded file.
- `status` warns about a broken config and a dormant pre-commit
  (`gateWarnings`, `bin/ssdd.mjs:700-714`). The session view doesn't
  mention a dormant pre-commit (`work-state.mjs:350-353`); today the harness
  gate does, on every commit (`review-gate.mjs:737-742`).

## Decisions

1. **The pre-commit is the review gate; the harness review gate goes.**
   - `review-gate.mjs`'s harness mode is removed (`:489-750`), with its
     PreToolUse entry in `settings-hooks.json` and its
     `beforeShellExecution` entry in `adapters/cursor/hooks.json`. Its
     shape checks, its repo walk and the `if` filter go with it, and so do
     `commandStart`, `gitInvocation` and `isCommit` in `git-cmd.mjs`.
   - Staging, stamping and committing can share one call on any harness.
     git runs the pre-commit on the index it really commits, in the repo it
     really commits to, so a worktree, a `cd` or `-a` is judged right.
   - `--pre-commit`'s block message names `--repo <its repo>` in the stamp
     command it prints, since it can't know the agent's cwd.
   - `SSDD_REVIEW_SKIP=1 git commit …` still works: the variable reaches the
     pre-commit.
   - A dormant pre-commit means no gate. `install` and `update` arm it as
     today; `status` and the session view (Decision 7) say when it's off.
2. **One way to stamp: `--stamp`, and it accepts a review run before
   `git add`.**
   - Completion stamps, `reviewGate.stamping` and `reviewerModels` are
     removed: the SubagentStart / SubagentStop entries, `subagentHook`,
     `readTranscript`, `parseVerdict`, `modelAllowed`, `model-id.mjs`, the
     dispatch files, the `refused` record, and git-guard's hooks-mode rule.
   - A stamp may name a routed file's work-tree content. An unstaged or
     untracked (not ignored) file is keyed as `git add` would key it:
     `srcMode:srcBlob` from `git ls-tree HEAD`, `dstMode:dstBlob` from its
     file mode and `git hash-object --path`. A later `git add` of the same
     content stages the same key, so the stamp holds. `--stamp` refuses
     only a file that's neither changed nor routed.
   - The reviewer contracts' input becomes `git diff HEAD` for the routed
     files (staged and unstaged), or the range the orchestrator names.
3. **A comment-only change carries a clean stamp forward.**
   - When reviewer R's stamped blob and the staged blob of file F differ
     only in comments, R's stamp still meets the gate, provided:
     - the HEAD side and both modes are unchanged, and the stamped blob
       still exists (`deltaFor`'s `'gone'` case doesn't carry);
     - R's stamp records no open issues (with v3.5, no open finding of R's
       on F). A reviewer that flagged something on F re-reviews F: it's the
       one who can say it's fixed;
     - R isn't the comment reviewer.
   - The comment reviewer, `reviewGate.commentReviewer` (default
     `docs-sync-reviewer`), still owes F and gets the delta as today. When
     it isn't routed to F, nothing carries.
   - It's computed in `judge()`, stateless: the stamp stays on its old key
     and each judgment compares the stripped blobs again, so `--check` and
     `--pre-commit` stay read-only. The triage note says which stamps
     carried.
   - **Comment-only** means byte-equal after stripping comments, trailing
     whitespace and blank lines. Conservative:
     - Only the JS/TS family (`.js .mjs .cjs .jsx .ts .tsx .mts .cts`). Any
       other extension is never comment-only.
     - Strings, template literals and regex literals are tokenized before
       comments; anything the scanner can't classify makes the change code.
     - A comment a tool reads is code: shebang, `eslint-`, `@ts-`,
       `prettier-ignore`, `c8` / `istanbul ignore`, `/*#__PURE__*/`,
       `/// <reference`, `//# sourceMappingURL`, and JSDoc type tags in a
       `.js`-family file.
   - docs-sync's contract gains a section: on a comment-only delta, check
     each changed comment's claim against the code it describes. That's the
     class plan 35's rounds caught (Evidence 4).
4. **git-guard blocks only what keeps the pre-commit running and what goes
   out.**
   - Blocks stay for `commit -n` / `--no-verify` and the plain
     `core.hooksPath` writes: `git -c core.hooksPath=…`, and `git config`
     naming the key with a value after it or with a spelled-out write
     subcommand or option (`set`, `unset`, `--unset`, `--unset-all`,
     `--add`, `--replace-all`, `--edit`). Reads pass. `extraRules` stays,
     with the force-push rule in the example config.
   - `git add -A` / `.` / `--all` and `commit --amend` are allowed with a
     warning that says what to do instead.
   - Removed: the `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` entry and git-guard's
     file-path check (`:58-64`), the env forms, abbreviated options and the
     shell-expansion rule. Each returns with the incident that shows an
     agent using it.
   - The four `gitGuard.block*` toggles go: with two blocks left, both
     load-bearing, there's nothing to turn off.
   - `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS=… git commit` turns the pre-commit off and now
     passes everything. No agent has written it; `docs/limitations.md`
     records it.
5. **Lint findings warn at commit time.** The pre-commit prints convention
   lint's findings and continues: `--staged` exits 0, or the pre-commit
   stops treating its exit as fatal. Edit-time lint (the PostToolUse /
   `afterFileEdit` hook) is unchanged; it only shows findings earlier.
6. **The config loses what no project set.**
   - Removed: `reviewGate.stamping`, `reviewGate.reviewerModels`,
     `reviewGate.exclude` (a route's own `exclude` stays),
     `preCommit.blockUntracked` (the untracked check stays a warning),
     `gitGuard.block*`, and `modelReview.generation` with its session line.
     The new-model checklist stays in README.
   - Added: `reviewGate.commentReviewer` (Decision 3).
   - A config that still has a removed key works; the key is ignored and
     `status` names it as obsolete. A config isn't broken for having one.
7. **`status` and the session view say what's off; nothing rewrites a
   project-owned file.**
   - For each installed adapter whose wiring is seeded (Claude Code's
     `.claude/settings.json`), `status` and the end of `update` list the
     template's hook entries the project lacks, with what each runs, and
     the entries the template dropped as safe to remove (Decisions 1, 2
     and 4 drop four).
   - The session view gains one line when the pre-commit is dormant, with
     the command to arm it. It replaces the harness gate's per-commit note.
   - Nothing in the gate depends on a hook event being wired: a missing one
     costs only the convenience it adds.

**What's left of the harness wiring.** Claude Code: SessionStart (the work
view), PreToolUse(Bash) git-guard and prod-guard, PreToolUse(`mcp__.*`)
prod-guard, PostToolUse(Edit|Write) convention-lint: 5 entries, from 9.
Cursor: `sessionStart`, `beforeShellExecution` git-guard and prod-guard,
`beforeMCPExecution` prod-guard, `afterFileEdit` convention-lint: 5, from 6.

**Interactions with v3.5** (unbuilt; v3.4 doesn't depend on it, but v3.5
does depend on what v3.4 removes):
- v3.5 Decision 2 parses findings at SubagentStop. With completion stamps
  gone, `--stamp --report <file>` is its only path, and v3.5's Open 1
  (`stamping: "hooks"` by default) is moot. v3.5 was revised to match on
  2026-10-30 (Open 3).
- A carried stamp isn't a review: it doesn't count as a v3.5 round and keeps
  R's findings. Since a stamp with open findings doesn't carry, a comment
  fix to R's own finding goes back to R, whose `✅ [<id>] fixed` closes it.
- v3.5's triage note and round-cap warning print from `--pre-commit`, which
  is where the gate now speaks.

## Scope

**In:**
- review-gate: harness mode and completion stamps removed; work-tree keys
  in `--stamp`; the comment-only carry in `judge()` and the triage note;
  `--repo` in the pre-commit's block message.
- A comment scanner for the JS/TS family, no dependencies, in
  `mechanisms/hooks/`. `model-id.mjs` removed; `git-cmd.mjs` loses three
  functions.
- git-guard: amend and bulk add as warnings; the file-path check, the
  hooks-mode rule, the env / abbreviation / expansion rules and the
  toggles removed; header comment updated.
- `convention-lint --staged` warns; the pre-commit continues.
- `ssdd-config.mjs`: the removed keys ignored and reported; the new key.
- `work-state.mjs`: the dormant-pre-commit line; the model-generation line
  removed.
- `bin/ssdd.mjs`: the wiring report in `status` and `update`.
- Adapters: `settings-hooks.json` loses four entries; Cursor's `hooks.json`
  loses one.
- The five framework reviewers and the domain template: input `git diff
  HEAD`. 3.3.2 rewrites their report blocks (branch
  `claude/3-3-2-process-text-e5f22e`, `eca0a4f`), so these edits start from
  that text. docs-sync's comment-claim section.
- `config.example.json`, README (threat model, the gate's layers),
  `SDD.md` §4 (one call can stage, stamp and commit; stamping before `git
  add`), `docs/limitations.md`, the selftests and CHANGELOG.

**Out:**
- Comment-only for other languages. Each needs its own scanner and the
  same "unsure is code" rule.
- Prose-only changes in a routed doc: its reviewers are routed to the prose
  on purpose.
- `paths` (Hatedate's migration may need it), `maxRoutedFiles` (measured),
  `extraRules`, `productionGuard` and the Supabase pack (outward-facing).
- prod-guard's shell reading (`shell-view.mjs`): it guards production, and
  it builds on `git-cmd`'s tokenizer rather than duplicating it.
- `/skills-audit` (never run in prizma; `docs/BACKLOG.md` → Later already
  asks to revisit it).
- The 3.3.2 quick fixes.

**Footprint:** removes about 370 lines of `review-gate.mjs` (harness mode
and completion stamps), `model-id.mjs`, about 30 lines of `git-cmd.mjs`,
about 45 lines of git-guard, two test files (752 lines) and parts of three
more, four Claude Code hook entries, one Cursor entry, and nine config keys.
Adds one scanner, one key function, one config key and two warnings. No new
hook event, no new git hook, no new block.

## Open

**Resolved by the owner, 2026-10-30:** every item below as my call: (1)
accept, (2) option (a), (3) v3.5 revised, (4) warn, (5) v3.4 before v3.5,
both before the migrations.

1. **Removing the harness gate leaves a dormant repo ungated.** Today the
   harness gate is the only gate where `core.hooksPath` isn't set (a fresh
   clone before `install`/`update`, or a user who unset it). After v3.4 the
   session view and `status` say so, and nothing blocks. My call: accept
   it. That's the owner's rule, a local commit can be undone, and the
   `prepare` script (`bin/ssdd.mjs:364-366`) arms a fresh clone on `npm
   install`.
2. **Decision 3's evidence is mixed.** Plan 35's comment-only rounds were
   costly and also caught wrong claims, from resilience, bias-semantics and
   the task reviewer. Clean stamps carrying, plus docs-sync checking comment
   claims, recovers some of that: a reviewer that was clean on F won't see
   a new wrong comment on F. Options: (a) as decided; (b) carry only for
   comment deletions and whitespace; (c) drop Decision 3. My call: (a).
3. **v3.5 needed a revision.** Its finding parse sat in a hook v3.4
   removes. Resolved (owner, 2026-10-30): v3.5 now reads findings from
   `--stamp --report`, and v3.4 is built first.
4. **Bulk add as a warning.** `git add -A` can stage a secret that a later
   push publishes, and no check stands at the push. My call: warn, since
   the agent reads the warning before it commits and the staged list is in
   the commit output; if the owner wants a push-time check, that's its own
   item.
5. **Sequencing with the migrations.** The migrations wait for v3.5 (owner,
   2026-10-22). With Open 3, v3.4 comes before v3.5, so before the
   migrations too, and each project migrates onto the smaller gate once.

## Clarify pass

Sources: this branch at `7507dec` (3.3.2 merged in), scratch repos on git
2.54.0 in the session scratchpad, prizma (`a84124c`) and Hatedate read-only,
the Claude Code hooks reference and Cursor's hooks page. All checked
2026-10-30. Line numbers are at `7507dec`.

1. **3.3.2 shipped part of this.** It reached `main` (`9bfacde`) after the
   Evidence was gathered, and is merged here. Already true:
   - The pre-commit runs every step and fails if any failed
     (`pre-commit:8-27`). So Decision 5 changes only `convention-lint
     --staged`: it prints its findings and exits 0. A file-list run (CI)
     still exits 1.
   - Edit-time lint warns under Claude Code, through
     `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (`convention-lint.mjs:26-30`).
   - Amend is allowed by default (`blockAmend: false`,
     `ssdd-config.mjs:48`). Decision 4 adds its warning and drops the
     toggle.
   - The session view names a dormant pre-commit (`work-state.mjs:362-366`)
     and the harness gate no longer does (`review-gate.mjs:744`). What's
     left of Decision 7's session line is the stricter "armed" (Clarify 6).
   - The reviewer report blocks are rewritten (`eca0a4f`). Decision 2's
     input edits start from that text.
   - The example config sets `reviewGate.exclude` to the test-file filter
     (`\.test\.`, `__tests__/`), and its routes are narrower. **Ruling**
     (owner, 2026-10-30): remove the key as Decision 6 says; no repo has
     seeded 3.3.2. The example config puts the filter in each route's own
     `exclude`. A config that still has the key: ignored, and `status` and
     `update` name it as obsolete (Decisions 6, 7).
   - With the narrower example routes, docs-sync covers only
     `package.json`, `server/routes/` and `.env.example`, so in a repo
     seeded from the example the carry (Decision 3) applies to those files
     only. prizma routes docs-sync to `^src/`, where the comment edits are.
2. **The scanner's grammar, prototyped and run on history.** A 415-line
   prototype, checked against an oracle: TypeScript's printer with
   `removeComments` (prizma's `node_modules/typescript`).
   - **Tokens.** `'…'` and `"…"` with escapes (a raw newline is
     unclassifiable); template literals with nested `${…}`, by recursion;
     regex literals with `\` escapes and `[…]` classes (a newline is
     unclassifiable); `//` ends at a line terminator, U+2028 or U+2029. Any
     unterminated construct, or a bracket left open or mismatched at the
     end (`()[]{}` on one stack), is unclassifiable.
   - **Regex or division.** A regex may start at the start, after an
     operator or punctuator other than `)` `]` `}`, after a `)` that closes
     `if` / `while` / `for` / `with`, and after `return typeof instanceof in
     of new delete void throw case do else yield await` unless a `.` or
     `?.` precedes the keyword. After an identifier, number, string,
     template, regex, `)`, `]` or a TS `x!`, `/` is division, across a
     newline too (as JS parses it). `<<` and `<=` are one token.
   - **After `}` or `++` / `--`, a bare `/` is unclassifiable.** The tokens
     can't tell a block's `}` from an object's, and the two readings
     tokenize differently. Cost: 0 pairs in either history, 2 of 18,451
     `node_modules` files (both minified).
   - **JSX**, in `.js .jsx .tsx .mjs .cjs` (the files TypeScript parses with
     JSX on): `<` in expression position followed by an identifier or `>`
     opens it; any other `<` there is unclassifiable, so a `.tsx` generic
     (`<T,>`, `<T extends …>`) is. Tag names may hold `. : -`; attribute
     strings have no escapes and stay byte for byte; `{…}` and `{...x}` are
     scanned as JS; comments between attributes are stripped. Children's
     text, up to `<` or `{`, is code (`<p>// hi</p>` stays); `{/* c */}`
     becomes `{}`. Closing names must match.
   - **Whitespace**, wider than Decision 3's sentence and each checked by
     the oracle: a removed block comment takes the spaces on one side
     (`f(a, /* x */ b)` equals `f(a, b)`); it leaves one space where it was
     the only boundary (`a/**/b` is `a b`), none beside `()[]{};,`; one
     holding a line break leaves `\n` (for ASI). `\r` is trailing
     whitespace in code, so CRLF to LF is comment-only. A missing final
     newline doesn't count. Strings, templates and JSX text are never
     trimmed, and an indent change is code.
   - **Comments a tool reads are code:** a `#!` at offset 0; `eslint-`
     (`disable`, `enable`, `env`), a body starting `eslint `, `/* global
     */`, `/* globals */`, `/* exported */`, `jshint`, `jslint`; `@ts-`;
     `prettier-ignore`; `c8`, `istanbul` and `v8 ignore`; `node:coverage`;
     `#__PURE__`, `@__PURE__`, `__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__`; `///` followed by
     `<`; `//# sourceMappingURL=` and `sourceURL=` (and `//@`); `@jsx…`;
     `@flow`, `@noflow`; `webpack…:` and `turbopack…:` magic comments;
     `@vite-ignore`; `/*!`, `@license`, `@preserve`; `biome-ignore`,
     `deno-lint-ignore`, `deno-fmt-ignore`, `dprint-ignore`, `oxlint-`,
     `tslint:`; `@refresh`; `@vitest-environment`, `@jest-environment`;
     `@format`, `@prettier`; and `ssdd-lint-ignore`, which SSDD's own lint
     reads (`convention-lint.mjs:80`; found in SSDD's history). In `.js
     .mjs .cjs .jsx` only, a `/**` block with `@template @typedef @callback
     @import @overload @enum @this @private @protected @public @readonly`,
     or with `@type @param @arg @argument @return(s) @satisfies @prop(erty)
     @extends @augments @implements` and a `{`, since `checkJs` reads it.
   - **The history.** Every modified file of those extensions with an
     unchanged mode, deduped by blob pair:

     | | SSDD (321 pairs, all `.mjs`) | prizma (1,441: 1,108 `.ts`, 299 `.tsx`, 34 other) |
     |---|---|---|
     | comment-only, oracle equal | 11 | 210 (187 `.ts`, 23 `.tsx`) |
     | comment-only, oracle different | **0** | **0** |
     | code, oracle equal | 0 | 0 |
     | code, oracle different | 310 | 1,231 |
     | unclassifiable | 0 | 0 |

     No pair it calls comment-only is a code change, and it misses none the
     oracle calls equal. Per blob, the oracle prints each blob and its
     stripped text the same: 2,114 history blobs, 18,451 prizma
     `node_modules` files, and 2,174 more `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.jsx` files from
     the owner's other repos, 0 mismatches.
   - **What the oracle can't check:** it drops every comment, so the
     tool-read list rests on 89 hand cases. Two of its rules cost nothing
     here but may elsewhere: the JSDoc rule fires without knowing whether a
     project sets `checkJs`, and `/*!` / `@license` make a license-header
     edit code. Both fail toward review.
   - Fixed during the run, none a false comment-only: `<<` read as JSX
     (345 spurious unclassifiable files in `node_modules`), and a NUL byte
     treated as unclassifiable (4 prizma pairs, `.join("\0")`).
3. **A comment line that only moves is comment-only already.** Stripping
   drops every comment, so no rule is needed, and docs-sync still gets the
   delta: a moved comment may now describe other code. Of the 221
   comment-only pairs, 1 only moved a comment (prizma `28337e4`), 1 only
   deleted blank lines, 4 add comments, 1 deletes one, and 214 edit comment
   text.
4. **Work-tree keys come from a scratch index, not `hash-object`.**
   - `git hash-object --path` matched `git add` on an `eol=lf` attribute
     and on `core.autocrlf=true`. It doesn't on a symlink: it hashed the
     target's content (`b5eff57`) where `git add` stores the link text
     (`3c1d453`, mode 120000). The mode would also need `core.fileMode`.
   - So `--stamp` asks git: it copies the index (`git rev-parse
     --git-path index`) to a temporary file in the git dir, runs
     `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A --pathspec-from-file=-
     --pathspec-file-nul` on the routed changed paths, reads the keys with
     the same `diff --cached --raw` parse as `stagedChanges`, and removes
     the file. The changed paths are `git diff HEAD --name-only` plus `git
     ls-files --others --exclude-standard`.
   - In a scratch repo its keys equal a real `git add`'s for: CRLF under
     `eol=lf`, `core.autocrlf=true`, an exec bit, `core.fileMode=false`, a
     symlink re-pointed, a deletion, an untracked file, and a clean filter
     (`tr a-z A-Z`; LFS is a clean filter, and git-lfs isn't installed
     here). An ignored path is refused by `git add` (exit 1), and `--stamp`
     refuses it too.
   - The temporary `add` writes the blobs. The delta line and the carry
     need that: `deltaFor` checks the stamped blob exists (`cat-file -e`,
     `review-gate.mjs:276`).
   - A stopped merge: the merge-clean rule runs on the scratch index the
     same way (`mergeClean` takes the index to read).
5. **A file staged, then edited, has two keys: `--stamp` names the work
   tree's.** That's what `git diff HEAD` showed the reviewer. When the
   index holds another blob, `--stamp` says so (`stamped the work-tree
   copy; the staged copy differs — git add it`), and the commit stays owed
   until it's added. One rule, no flag, and it fails closed.
6. **"Armed" means the pre-commit git runs calls the gate.**
   - prizma's and Hatedate's `core.hooksPath` are both set, to absolute
     paths of their own `.githooks`, and both have a `pre-commit`. prizma's
     runs `review-gate.mjs --pre-commit` (its line 25, a customized copy);
     Hatedate's 163-line one never has.
   - So a hash of the lock's managed entry can't be the test: a project
     edits its pre-commit and `update` merges it. The test is the text:
     the `pre-commit` in the resolved `core.hooksPath` matches
     `/review-gate\.mjs\b[^\n]*--pre-commit/`.
   - `dormantHook` gains the reason `its pre-commit doesn't run the review
     gate`; `status`, `update` and the session view already call it. A
     linked worktree running the main checkout's copy (`foreignHook`)
     still matches. A wrapper (a husky hook that calls
     `.githooks/pre-commit`) reads as dormant: a false line, never a
     block, and the reason names the file.
7. **How a warning reaches the agent from a hook that allows.**
   - Claude Code: "Claude never sees stderr from a hook that exits 0"
     (hooks reference). Only `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`
     reaches the model on an allowed PreToolUse call, as the triage note
     already does (`review-gate.mjs:750`). git-guard's `finish` gains that
     branch, and still prints nothing on a plain allow.
   - Cursor: `beforeShellExecution` documents `agent_message` on a deny
     only; on an allow it's undocumented. **Ruling** (owner, 2026-10-30):
     the same warning on every harness, best effort on Cursor
     (`{"permission":"allow","agent_message":…}`). `docs/limitations.md`
     says Cursor may not show it.
8. **`status` matches a hook entry by event, matcher and script.**
   - A project entry matches a template entry when the event is the
     same, the matcher covers the template's (equal, every `|`
     alternative of the template's among the project's, or the project's
     empty or `*`), and a command names the script's file name
     (`git-guard.mjs`), whatever path, env prefix or arguments surround
     it. `if` filters are ignored.
   - Missing: a template entry nothing matches, with its event, matcher
     and script. Safe to remove: a project command naming an
     `.ssdd/hooks/*.mjs` script where the template has no entry for that
     script on that event and matcher. Both lists come from the template,
     not a list in code; v3.4's template yields the four of Decision 7.
   - `status` compares with the template at the lock's commit, `update`
     with the new one. Only Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` is
     seeded; Cursor's `hooks.json` is managed and merged, and the generic
     adapter wires nothing.
9. **Stale wiring is harmless.** Until a project edits its
   `.claude/settings.json`, Claude Code still calls `review-gate.mjs` on
   PreToolUse(Bash), SubagentStart and SubagentStop, and git-guard on file
   edits.
   - `review-gate.mjs` with no mode exits 0 and prints nothing, except
     `{"permission":"allow"}` for a Cursor payload: a `failClosed` entry
     left in a customized `.cursor/hooks.json` would otherwise block every
     shell call.
   - git-guard on an Edit/Write payload finds no command and allows.
10. **The selftests that move before the two files go.**
    - From `review-gate.shapes.selftest.mjs`: `--stamp … --repo <path>
      unblocks that repo from anywhere` (`:328`, now `--stamp --repo`,
      then `--check --repo` and `--pre-commit` in the repo); the worktree
      block's `--stamp --repo <wt>` (`:369`, then `--pre-commit` in the
      worktree) and `--pre-commit judges git's cwd, not a decoy in the env`
      (`:375`); and `route exclude` (`:382-399`), whose `reviewGate.exclude`
      case becomes "an obsolete `reviewGate.exclude` is ignored".
    - From `review-stamp.selftest.mjs`: the triage note (`:267`, now
      `--pre-commit` with an `issues: 1` entry the test writes into the
      stamp file, since nothing in v3.4 writes one; Clarify 14); `two
      reviewers finishing at once both land` (`:191`, now two parallel
      `--stamp` runs: the lock stays); and the guard's config cases
      (`:338-350`, into `git-guard.selftest.mjs`: an unstaged `extraRules`
      entry applies; a broken config keeps `--no-verify` blocked, and
      `add -A` and `--amend` warn).
    - New, in place of the shape cases: real commits through an armed
      pre-commit (`armPreCommit`, `review-gate.selftest.mjs:954`). `commit
      -am`, `commit <path>`, `git add f && git commit` in one shell string,
      and `git -C <worktree> commit` are each blocked on what git commits,
      and pass after `--stamp`.
    - Deleted with their code: the command-shape, repo-walk, two-repo and
      commit-detection cases, and every completion-stamp, model, handback,
      hooks-mode and Edit/Write case.
    - In files that stay: `review-gate.selftest.mjs`'s harness-mode cases
      (`:91`, `:100-116`, `:355-419`, `:464`, `:637`, `:911-966`, and
      `:968`, which becomes "a shell hand-off is judged by git's
      pre-commit"); `git-guard.selftest.mjs:221-226`, `:256`, `:272`;
      `ssdd-config.selftest.mjs:67-90`, `:282-314`;
      `work-state.selftest.mjs:917-940`; `bin/ssdd.selftest.mjs:592` (the
      `if` filter, now "no template wires review-gate");
      `bin/repo.selftest.mjs:224` (the completion-stamp sentence).
11. **Codex and other harnesses.** With no adapter they read `AGENTS.md`,
    meet the pre-commit at `git commit`, and run the CLI (`--check`,
    `--stamp`, `work-state.mjs`). After v3.4 that is the whole gate on
    every harness; Claude Code and Cursor add git-guard, prod-guard,
    edit-time lint and the session view on top. Nothing else differs.
    `AGENTS.md`'s "commit in a separate call" goes.
12. **Version 3.4.0, MINOR.** Removed keys are ignored. The stamp file
    stays version 2: `by`, `verdict`, `model` and `refused` are no longer
    written, and readers never needed them. No project-owned file is
    rewritten, and stale wiring is harmless (Clarify 9). CHANGELOG's
    Upgrade (optional): remove the entries `status` lists and the keys it
    names.
13. **Seven reviewer files read `git diff --staged`, not six.** The five
    framework reviewers, the domain template and `gate-reviewer.md` (`:27`).
    All seven take `git diff HEAD` for their routed files.
14. **No v3.4 stamp records issues.** Completion stamps were the only
    writer of `issues` (`review-gate.mjs:863`); `--stamp` writes `{ key, at
    }`. A manual stamp comes after "fix or triage, then stamp" (SDD.md §4
    step 3), so Decision 3's "no open issues" holds for every v3.4 stamp by
    the contract. The carry still checks `issues > 0`, so v3.5's findings
    plug into the same check. The triage note's flagged lines have no
    writer until v3.5 either; they stay, and the note gains the
    carried-stamp lines.

## Deviations & discoveries

What shipped differs from the Decisions and Clarify items in these ways.
Each is a `Ruling:` in `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-30-v3-4-gate-in-git/progress.md`
with its cost if wrong. Costs below are measured over the AC7 runs: pairs
lost on history, files nulled the prototype classified (1,589 tracked /
18,464 `node_modules` / 1,103 `.tsx`/`.jsx`).

- **Clarify 2 was wrong about `/` across a newline (R13).** "After an
  identifier … `/` is division, across a newline too (as JS parses it)" is
  not how JS parses it: ASI depends on what follows, so `x = a\n/re/.test(s)`
  can't be told from a division by tokens alone. A `/`, or a JSX-opening
  `<`, after a line break following a value is unclassifiable
  (`comment-strip.mjs:279`, `:293`). Cost: `/` 0 / 0 / 0 / 0; `<` 0 / 0 /
  3 / 0 (protobufjs, a line-leading `< 128`).
- **Other null-widening rulings** (`comment-strip.mjs`), each found by
  review or fuzzing against TypeScript, never by history:
  - R14 `<!--` anywhere, `-->` first on its line (`:285-286`): 0 everywhere.
  - R15 `/` after `of` / `yield` / `await`, which may be identifiers
    (`MAYBE_ID`, `:37`): 0 everywhere.
  - R16 a kept next-line directive (`eslint-disable-next-line`, `@ts-*`,
    `prettier-ignore`, …) with a comment or blank line removed below it
    (`NEXT_LINE`, `:75`); R19, R21 a kept `ignore next N` with any line
    removed below it (`COUNTED`, `:78`): history 1 pair; files 3 / 102 /
    4. Of the 102, 28 aren't aimed at a line (below).
  - R17 a `<` in a JSX file after `}`, an ambiguous token or a line break
    (`:293`): counted with R13's `<`.
  - R20 a `<` after `extends` in a JSX file (`:294`): 0 everywhere.
  - R22 a `.tsx` tag followed by `(`, or holding `,`, `extends` or `=`
    before an attribute name (`:399`, `:406`, `:425`): history 0 pairs (4
    code pairs, 5 blobs, now unclassifiable); files 3 / 0 / 0.
  - R23 a `\` in a `.tsx` attribute string (`:417`): 0 everywhere.
  - Any U+FFFD (a non-UTF-8 blob) is unclassifiable (`:458`): history 0
    pairs; files 0 / 28 / 0.
- **`NEXT_LINE` matches any kept comment holding the word "ignore".** The
  one carry lost on real history is SSDD's own `convention-lint.mjs`
  (`222ded0`): its header line names `ssdd-lint-ignore`, which is
  tool-read, and `\bignore\b` makes it a next-line directive, so the next
  removed comment line nulls the file. `ssdd-lint-ignore` is a same-line
  marker. In `node_modules`, 11 nulls are `c8 ignore start` (a range) and
  17 are other kept comments that mention `ignore`, 13 of them JSDoc blocks. It costs reviews, never a
  wrong carry. Open: narrow `NEXT_LINE`, or keep it.
- **The grammar grew beyond Clarify 2's lists**, each toward code:
  `default` and `extends` start an expression (`EXPR_KW`, `:33`, R18);
  Flow comment types (`/*: T */`, `/*:: */`), `deno-coverage-ignore*` and
  JSDoc `@constructor` / `@class` / `@override` in `.js` are tool-read
  (`:66`, `:71`, `:79`); the coverage and deno patterns ignore case. An
  esbuild `//!` legal comment is still stripped; `Function.prototype.toString`
  is in `docs/limitations.md`.
- **Only a regular file carries (R24).** The carry needs mode `100644` or
  `100755` on the new side (`review-gate.mjs:382`): a symlink's blob is its
  target, which strips like code. Decision 3 didn't say it. Symlinks and
  gitlinks never carry.
- **`--stamp`'s path list always adds `git diff --cached --name-only`
  (R5).** Clarify 4 listed `git diff HEAD --name-only` and `ls-files
  --others`; a staged change put back in the work tree is in neither, and
  its staged blob must not be keyed (`review-gate.mjs:190-196`). The
  HEAD side reads `diff-index`, which never refreshes the real index (R6).
  The scratch index keeps the real index's mtime, so a same-size edit in
  the stage's second stays racy (`:213`), and pathspecs are literal
  (`GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1`, `:223`, R7). That list also holds a staged
  deletion (`git rm`, `git mv`'s old name, `rm --cached` of a file now
  ignored), which is in neither the index nor the non-ignored work tree, and
  `add` is fatal on it: only paths the scratch index or `ls-files --others`
  holds go to `add` (`:215-220`); the copied index already records the
  rest. A git failure there prints git's message and one line, exit 1.
- **Lint at commit warns, per Decision 5.** `--staged` exits 0 on a
  finding; a config it can't read, or a rule that doesn't compile, still
  exits 1 and fails the commit (`convention-lint.mjs:48-49`;
  `pre-commit:14-17`). A file-list run exits 1 on a finding.
- **"Armed" is a line that isn't a comment (R12).** Clarify 6's regex is
  applied per line, skipping lines that start with `#`
  (`ssdd-config.mjs:204`). A trailing comment (`echo x # review-gate.mjs
  --pre-commit`) still reads as armed.
- **The dormant line gives the fix, not only the reason (R10).** For
  "doesn't run the review gate" it names the line to add and the file,
  even for SSDD's own copy, since `update` keeps a local edit to it; for an
  unset path, `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` (`dormantHookDetail`,
  `ssdd-config.mjs:218`). Decision 7 asked for "the command to arm it",
  and setting `core.hooksPath` doesn't arm a pre-commit that never calls
  the gate.
- **Clarify 6's premise that `update` calls `dormantHook` was wrong.** It
  calls `armHook` (`bin/ssdd.mjs:583`), which arms an unset path and is
  silent otherwise; only `status` prints the warning (`gateWarnings`,
  `:769`, called at `:826`). A 3.3.2 install whose `core.hooksPath` points
  at Hatedate's `.githooks`, updated to `2942b85`: no dormant line; `status`
  right after prints it, while `CHANGELOG.md:88` and
  `docs/limitations.md:20` say `update` names it. Fixed (R28): one helper
  (`dormantLine`, `bin/ssdd.mjs`) prints it for both, and `update` calls it
  after `armHook`, without the "rerun: update" hint.
- **"5 entries, from 9" counts handlers (R3).** Claude Code's template
  went from 7 entries holding 9 handlers to 4 holding 5.
- **AC3's grep isn't empty:** two selftests name `ssdd-review-dispatch` to
  check it's gone (AC3 above).
- **An obsolete global `reviewGate.exclude` routes test files again.**
  Ignored, as Decision 6 says, so the files it dropped reach their
  reviewers until the patterns move into each route's `exclude`. CHANGELOG
  calls it a behaviour change.
- **A removed key inside a wrong-typed section isn't named (R9).**
  `gitGuard: "x"` is reported as a config error already; its keys can't be
  read, so `status` names them one fix later.
- **`status` survives a lock commit the source lacks (R11).** It compares
  the wiring with the template at the lock's commit (Clarify 8) only when
  that commit is in the source checkout, and otherwise says so instead of
  crashing.
- **The installed selftests fail on a fresh install, since 3.3.2.**
  "the example hex-colour rule" and "the example config routes narrowly"
  read `.ssdd/config.example.json`, which install doesn't ship; three
  sibling tests skip when it's absent. A plain v3.3.2 install fails the
  same 3. Open.
- **The CHANGELOG is dated 2026-11-01 (R25)**, to be moved at release.
